name: Asylum -- Refugee Status Determination (DAARA / Commission Nationale d'Eligibilite)

qualifying_event.description: An asylum seeker in Cote d'Ivoire applies through the Direction d'Aide et d'Assistance aux Refugies et Apatrides (DAARA, formerly SAARA), under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which coordinates with the National Eligibility Commission (Commission Nationale d'Eligibilite, CNE) and an Appeals Commission (Commission de Recours, CR) and prefectural authorities for status determination.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Registration with DAARA at its offices in Abidjan, Tabou, Guiglo, Toulepleu, or Danane; evidence supporting a well-founded fear of persecution.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution, assessed by the National Eligibility Commission (CNE) in coordination with DAARA and prefectural authorities.

sources.title: DAARA (Direction d'Aide et d'Assistance aux Refugies et Apatrides, formerly SAARA), Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cote d'Ivoire -- refugee status determination via the National Eligibility Commission (CNE) and Appeals Commission (CR); refugee ID cards, travel documents, physical protection; offices in Abidjan, Tabou, Guiglo, Toulepleu, Danane; reintegration/monitoring support for voluntarily repatriated former refugees

STATUS: DRAFT -- fully tier-1 sourced (DAARA's own government page, .gouv.ci domain) but the page ITSELF states Cote d'Ivoire lacks a comprehensive domestic asylum LAW, describing only an 'avant-projet de loi sur l'asile' (draft asylum bill) as being prepared -- meaning the CNE/CR eligibility-determination structure currently operates on an administrative/institutional basis rather than a codified statute, a genuine structural finding disclosed rather than smoothed over. DATING CAVEAT: it is unclear from this pass whether that draft law has since been enacted -- the DAARA page is live and government-hosted but does not carry a visible last-updated date, and this dataset could not independently confirm current status against a more recent source; flagged as a high-priority re-verification item, similar in kind to this build's own family_reunification/investor_residence gaps and this dataset's Mongolia asylum finding. work_rights/study_rights/family_can_join/family_can_work are conservative defaults, not sourced figures -- the DAARA page describes refugee documentation and physical-protection guarantees but not specific work/study/family rights during or after the procedure.
